items.heading: Ui/ux Design Remains a Genuinely
items.text: UI/UX design remains a genuinely viable field in India, growing hard where products need real research and interaction judgment, and genuinely crowded at the exact entry point most beginners walk into first. It is not the oversaturated dead end some online chatter suggests, and it is also not the easy, work-from-anywhere creative career some bootcamp ads promise.

items.heading: Two True Things Are Happening
items.text: Two true things are happening in UI/UX design in India at the same time, and most articles only tell you one of them, which is why the honest answer feels contradictory.

items.heading: Before Comparing Pay or Tracks,
items.text: Before comparing pay or tracks, it helps to see the actual daily texture of the work, not the version that shows up in a bootcamp advertisement or a curated Dribbble portfolio.

rows: Junior UI/UX designer, bootcamp or self-taught, 0-2 years

Glassdoor's aggregated India range for 1-3 years puts entry offers between roughly Rs 3-7 LPA. The wide spread is city- and employer-driven: a small agency or service shop pays toward the bottom, a funded product startup or MNC pays toward the top for near-identical job titles.
UI/UX designer, mid-size product company or agency, 2-4 years

This is where the job stops being "make the screens someone else already decided on" and starts being "own a flow end to end, defend it with research, and hand off production-ready specs." That shift, not years alone, moves pay here.
Rs 10-18 LPA, higher at well-funded product companies

Glassdoor's experienced band (7-9+ years) runs roughly Rs 8-18 lakh or more. Senior pay tracks with ownership of a product area, mentoring juniors, and defending design decisions to leadership, not with additional years of pushing pixels.
UX researcher (dedicated research role, not a designer who also researches)
Rs 8-16 LPA, rising faster than pure-visual UI roles

A genuinely under-supplied specialisation in India relative to demand. Companies rolling out AI features specifically need someone who can test whether users trust and understand what the AI is doing, which is a research skill, not a visual one.

items.heading: There Is No Licensing Body
items.text: There is no licensing body for UI/UX designers in India, unlike architecture or medicine. Anyone can use the title and take paid work, which means the market decides credibility purely through visible, provable portfolio work, not a certificate, right as that market gets flooded with visually similar bootcamp portfolios.

items.heading: Generative AI Tools Have Moved
items.text: Generative AI tools have moved directly into the field's most common entry-level tasks, wireframing, first-draft layouts, boilerplate component production, faster than into most other creative-adjacent work.
